transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been having some trouble with eating. It’s embarrassing to say, because I know I should be able to handle it better, but sometimes once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it’s like I can’t quite make myself stop.

I’m telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away,” but it feels like I’ve sort of stepped aside and I’m not really in control. That probably sounds strange, but that’s the part that scares me.
Can you describe what happens when you feel like you can’t stop eating? Does this happen often, and do you feel like you’re eating a lot more than most people would in a similar situation?

It’s not every day, exactly… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it has happened enough that I’m worried.

Like, some afternoons after I’ve done a shift at the food bank, or if I’ve been baking for one of the senior-center events, I’ll come home and tell myself I’m just going to have a normal plate of leftovers. And then it sort of keeps going. I’ll have the leftovers, and then maybe a few slices of banana bread, and then chips, some cheese, cookies if there are any in the tin.

And at the time I keep thinking, “Okay, that’s enough,” but I don’t really stop. Afterward I’ll look at what I ate and think… I would never serve that much to another person as a meal. So yes, I guess it is a lot more than most people would probably eat in that situation.
After these episodes where you feel like you've eaten more than you intended, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really done those kinds of things, not making myself sick or anything like that.

I do feel awful afterward, and I might tell myself I should be more careful the next day, but I’m not sure that’s the same as what you mean. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do these episodes bother you a lot, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way, like making you avoid certain activities or feel ashamed?

It does bother me, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped doing things. I still go to my volunteer shifts, and I still do the craft fairs and things like that.

But I have started… sort of ducking out of some of the meals afterward, when everyone’s eating together. I feel embarrassed, and I worry people can tell I’m upset or that they’ll ask me what’s wrong. So I’ll make an excuse and leave. I know that’s probably not the best way to handle it.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control of your eating, like you can’t stop once you start?

Yes… I think that is what happens. I don’t like admitting it, because it sounds like I’m just not trying hard enough, but once I start—especially if I’m by myself in the kitchen—it feels like I’ve sort of stepped aside.

I’ll be telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away, that’s enough,” and I still keep reaching for things. It scares me a little, honestly, because in the moment I can’t seem to make myself stop.
Do these episodes ever cause you a lot of distress or make it hard for you to function in your daily life, like affecting your relationships or getting things done?

I wouldn’t say it keeps me from everything… I do still make myself go to my volunteer shifts, and I still do the craft fairs. I don’t want you to think I’ve just stopped my life or anything.

But, um… it has started affecting things a bit. If there’s a meal afterward, with the group, I’ve been making excuses not to stay. I feel embarrassed, and I worry people will notice I’m upset or ask me about it. So I just leave before that can happen. I guess that counts as interfering, doesn’t it?
Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you say you 'step aside' while eating — do you feel completely unable to stop, even when you want to?

Yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s what frightens me about it. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it’s like part of me knows very clearly I should stop.

I’ll be thinking, “Janet, put it away now, that’s enough,” and then my hand just keeps going back. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it in the normal way. I know that probably sounds silly, but in the moment I really can’t seem to make myself stop, even though I want to.

During these episodes, do you ever feel like you're completely detached from yourself, as if you're watching yourself eat but can't take control, or does it feel more like you're aware and making the choice, even if you wish you could stop?

It’s… I don’t know if I’d say I’m completely outside myself, like in a movie. I’m still aware it’s me, and I know what I’m doing.

But what scares me is that once I start, especially when I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I’ve sort of stepped aside. I’m telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away, that’s enough,” and somehow I still can’t make myself stop. I wish I could say it feels like a choice, but in the moment it really doesn’t feel that simple.
During these episodes, do you ever feel spaced out, detached, or as if things aren’t quite real, like you're in a dream or not fully present?

I’m not sure I’d describe it like a dream, no. I mean… I’m aware I’m there, and I know what I’m doing, even if I don’t feel very in control of it.

Maybe I get sort of focused or a little numb, but not like things aren’t real. At least, I haven’t noticed that exactly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these episodes, do you ever feel like you're not fully aware of what you're doing, or that it doesn't quite feel like it's really you eating?

I don’t think so… not exactly. I’m embarrassed by it, but I do know it’s me doing it. I’m aware enough to know what I’m eating and that I wish I would stop.

It’s more like I’m not listening to myself, if that makes sense, rather than I’m not really there. I hope I’m explaining that right.
During these episodes, do you ever feel like you're not fully connected to yourself, as if you're watching yourself from the outside, even just a little bit?

I don’t think I’ve felt like I’m watching myself from outside, no. At least not that I’ve noticed.

It’s more like I’m there and I know it’s me, I just feel… stuck in it, I guess. I don’t want to overstate it and make it sound more dramatic than it is. Is that okay to say?
During these episodes, do you ever feel like your awareness is changed, such as feeling like you're in a fog or not completely clear-headed, even if you know you're eating?

Maybe a little unclear in the sense that I’m upset or overwhelmed, but I don’t know if I’d call it a fog. I still know I’m eating and what’s happening.

I guess I haven’t really noticed my awareness changing like that. It’s more that I’m kind of caught up in it, if that makes sense. Is that an okay distinction?
Do you ever feel like you’ve lost control over your eating, like you can’t stop eating or manage what or how much you’re eating, even if it’s not during a binge episode?

Yes… I think that’s probably the part that bothers me the most, honestly.

I don’t want to make it sound like I have no responsibility for it, because I know I’m the one doing it, but once I start eating—especially if I’m alone in the kitchen—it feels like I can’t get myself to stop. I’ll be telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away,” and I still keep going.

It’s embarrassing to say that out loud. But yes, it does feel like I’m not managing what or how much I’m eating in those moments. Is that what you mean?
During these episodes, do you feel like you’ve completely lost control over your eating, like you can’t stop eating even though you want to, or do you feel like you could stop if you really tried?

I guess… I want to say I could stop if I really tried, because that sounds better. But in the moment, it really doesn’t feel that way.

What scares me is once I start eating, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it’s like I’ve kind of stepped aside and I can’t make myself stop, even though I’m telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away.” I know that probably sounds strange, but that’s what it feels like.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’ve completely lost control over your eating, like you can’t stop eating even though you want to, or do you feel like you could stop if you really tried?

I know I kind of already said this, but… in the moment, it feels more like I can’t stop, even though I want to.

I mean, maybe technically I could if I somehow snapped out of it, but when I’m alone in the kitchen and I start, it’s like I’ve stepped aside from myself. I’m telling myself, “Janet, put it away,” and I just… don’t. That’s the part that scares me.
